name: Lahori Chargha
description: Lahori-style whole chicken chargha marinated with yogurt, lemon and bold spices, gently steamed for tenderness and finished until richly browned.
ingredients: Chaat masala, lemon and chutney for serving
method: Pat the chicken dry and make several shallow cuts in the thickest fleshy areas so the marinade reaches more surface without cutting deeply into bone.
Mix the yogurt, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, red chilli, cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric, gram flour and salt into a smooth marinade. Rub it thoroughly over and inside the chicken.
Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours. Keep the raw chicken chilled until the cooking process begins.

Set the chicken on a steaming rack above simmering water, cover and steam steadily until the meat is nearly cooked through. Whole birds cook unevenly, so check the thickest breast and inner-thigh areas rather than judging only by time.
Carefully remove the chicken and let surface moisture evaporate. If frying, make the exterior as dry as practical before it approaches hot oil; alternatively roast to develop the browned finish.
Finish by frying or roasting until richly browned and fully cooked through, then rest for about 10 minutes before serving with chaat masala, lemon and chutney.
tips: A whole chicken can cook unevenly, so temperature is more reliable than appearance alone.
If deep frying after steaming, dry the exterior well and lower the chicken carefully to reduce dangerous oil splatter.
storage: Cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate covered. Reheat the portion being served until thoroughly hot.
image_alt: Lahori chargha whole chicken with bold yogurt spice marinade and deep browned finish
image_caption: Whole Lahori chargha marinated, steamed until nearly tender and finished until richly browned.
technique: Use the two-stage method for control: steam until the whole chicken is nearly cooked, then dry the exterior and finish with frying or roasting for colour. This separates internal doneness from crust development.
doneness_cues: Steamed chicken should be nearly cooked before browning begins.
Surface should lose visible moisture before hot-oil finishing.
Final exterior should be deep golden-red rather than black.
Thick breast and inner-thigh areas must be fully cooked before serving.
mistakes: Trying to cook a raw whole bird entirely by deep frying.
Moving a wet steamed bird straight into hot oil.
Using deep cuts that cause the bird to dry out.
Skipping temperature checks on a whole chicken.
substitutions: Roast after steaming instead of deep frying for a lower-oil finish.
Use less chilli while keeping cumin, coriander and garam masala.
A slightly smaller chicken cooks more evenly.
reheating: Reheat covered until hot through; finish uncovered briefly for surface texture.
serving: Rest 10 minutes, then serve with lemon, chutney and a light sprinkle of chaat masala.
